issues.title: Establish Core MCP Server with Go SDK
issues.objective: Set up the foundational Go project structure and integrate the official `github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk` to begin building the 'modex' MCP server, targeting Go 1.25+.
issues.problem: The 'modex' project needs a basic Go 1.25+ environment and the `go-sdk` to enable LLM-assisted Go development. This involves initializing a Go module, adding the SDK as a dependency, and creating a minimal MCP server bootstrap.
changes: Initialize a new Go module for 'modex' using `go mod init modex`.
Add `github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk` as a dependency to the Go module.
Create a `main.go` file with a minimal MCP server implementation (e.g., using `mcp.NewServer()` and `server.Serve(ctx)` for stdio transport).
issues.verification: Successfully run `go mod tidy` and compile `main.go` without errors. The minimal server should start and run without crashing.
out_of_scope: Implementing any specific MCP tools beyond the basic server framework.
Detailed error handling or complex server configurations.
acceptance_criteria: A valid `go.mod` and `go.sum` file exist.
The project successfully builds using `go build .`.
A basic MCP server can be executed from the `main.go` file.

new_tests: Verify that `go mod tidy` completes successfully after adding the SDK.
Confirm that the basic MCP server compiles and runs without panicking, indicating correct SDK integration.
testing_strategy.test_patterns: Standard Go testing practices using `_test.go` files and `go test ./...`.

risks: Compatibility issues with specific Go 1.25+ features if the SDK is not fully updated.
issues.notes: This issue is a foundational step for all subsequent MCP tool development.

references.title: go-sdk: The official Go SDK for Model Context Protocol servers and clients.
references.why: This is the official Go SDK for MCP, and its usage is a core constraint of the 'modex' project. This repository will be the primary reference for implementing the MCP server and client functionalities.

references.title: mcp-go: A Go implementation of the Model Context Protocol (MCP).
references.why: This project provides a concrete example of an MCP server implementation in Go. It can serve as a valuable reference for understanding the architecture and design patterns for building an MCP server using Go.

references.title: GopherCon 2025 presentation by Katie Hockman, 'Next-Gen AI Tooling with MCP Servers in Go'
references.why: This GopherCon presentation is a direct and highly relevant resource for understanding how to build MCP servers using the Go SDK. It will likely provide practical guidance, best practices, and potentially code examples for implementing the 'modex' server.

issues.title: Implement SQLite FTS5 for Go Documentation Indexing
issues.objective: Integrate SQLite with FTS5 to create a robust full-text search index for Go documentation, covering both the standard library and project dependencies.
issues.problem: 'modex' requires an efficient and comprehensive way to search Go documentation to assist LLMs. Utilizing SQLite with its FTS5 extension is the chosen approach, requiring initial database and table setup.
changes: Add `github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3` and `github.com/knaka/go-sqlite3-fts5` as Go module dependencies.
Create a dedicated internal Go package (e.g., `internal/docdb`) for database management.

Implement functions within `internal/docdb` to initialize an SQLite database and create an FTS5 table specifically for documentation entries (e.g., storing package path, symbol name, and documentation text).
Develop methods to insert and retrieve sample documentation data from the FTS5 table.
issues.verification: The SQLite database file should be created successfully. The FTS5 table should be verifiable. Basic FTS5 search queries against inserted sample data should return expected results.
out_of_scope: Crawling and populating the entire Go standard library and dependency documentation (addressed in a separate issue).
Advanced FTS5 features like ranking or custom tokenizers.
acceptance_criteria: A working SQLite database with an FTS5 table is created.
Go functions can insert and retrieve data from the FTS5 table.
Basic full-text searches yield correct results for sample data.

new_tests: Test database initialization: ensure a valid SQLite database file is created at the specified path.
Test FTS5 table creation: verify the table schema includes FTS5 specific columns and properties.
Test document insertion: insert several dummy documentation entries and confirm they are stored.
Test basic FTS5 search: execute simple keyword searches against the dummy data and assert correct retrieval.
testing_strategy.test_patterns: Standard Go testing practices using `_test.go` files and `go test ./...`.

research_questions: What is the optimal schema for storing Go documentation (e.g., fields for package, type, function, description) to maximize search relevance?
risks: Performance bottlenecks with FTS5 on very large documentation datasets if not optimized correctly.
Complexity of managing SQLite database file paths and concurrency.
issues.notes: This issue lays the groundwork for the `search_docs` MCP tool.

references.title: engram: Persistent memory system for AI coding agents. Agent-agnostic Go binary with SQLite + FTS5, MCP server, HTTP API, CLI, and TUI.
references.why: Engram is highly relevant as it demonstrates a complete implementation of a persistent memory system for AI agents using SQLite with FTS5 and also functions as an MCP server. This project provides a strong architectural and technical reference for 'modex''s documentation search and indexing component.

references.why: This utility directly addresses the need to crawl and bundle documentation with full-text search. It's a valuable reference for implementing 'modex''s FTS5 index for Go documentation (stdlib + dependencies) and integrating with `go doc`.

references.title: go-sqlite3-fts5: Importing this package will enable the FTS5 extension with github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3 package.
references.why: This package is a critical technical dependency for enabling FTS5 with the `github.com/mattn/go-sqlite3` library in Go. It directly supports the constraint of using SQLite with FTS5 for documentation storage and search.

references.title: Real-Time Full-Text Site Search with SQLite FTS5 extension
references.why: This Hacker News discussion highlights the practical application and efficiency of SQLite's FTS5 for full-text search. issues.title: Implement MCP Tool: `get_diagnostics` (Consolidated Report)
issues.objective: Create a high-level `get_diagnostics` MCP tool that orchestrates calls to various Go tooling to provide a comprehensive diagnostic report to LLMs.
issues.problem: LLMs require consolidated feedback on Go code quality, including potential compilation issues, linting warnings, `go vet` issues, security vulnerabilities, and modernization opportunities. A unified diagnostic tool is needed to streamline this process.
changes: Define the `get_diagnostics` tool within the MCP server, accepting parameters such as target file paths or module roots.
Implement the tool's logic to internally invoke (or prepare for invoking) `go vet`, an external Go linter (e.g., Staticcheck), `govulncheck`, and `go fix -diff` for modernization insights.
Aggregate the results from these individual diagnostic tools into a single, structured diagnostic report.
Design a clear, LLM-friendly output format for the consolidated report, including error/warning type, message, and location (file, line, column).
issues.verification: The `get_diagnostics` tool should successfully gather and present a consolidated report of all identified issues when run on a sample Go project with various known code quality problems.
out_of_scope: Full implementation of each individual diagnostic tool (these are covered in separate issues or rely on external tools).
Real-time diagnostic updates; this tool provides a snapshot.
acceptance_criteria: The `get_diagnostics` MCP tool is registered and callable.
When run on a Go project, the tool returns a consolidated report that includes simulated output from `go vet`, a linter, `govulncheck`, and `go fix -diff`.
The report correctly categorizes and formats different types of diagnostic messages.

new_tests: Create a sample Go file with known `go vet` issues and verify `get_diagnostics` correctly reports them.
Create a sample Go file with known linting issues (simulated) and verify `get_diagnostics` includes them in the report.
Test `get_diagnostics` on a clean Go file to ensure no false positives or empty reports.
testing_strategy.test_patterns: Standard Go testing practices using `_test.go` files and `go test ./...`.

research_questions: What is the most effective way to integrate and parse output from diverse Go tooling (`go vet`, linters, `govulncheck`) into a consistent internal data structure?
How can we minimize the overhead of running multiple diagnostic tools for each `get_diagnostics` call?
risks: Parsing diverse tool outputs can be brittle and prone to breakage with tool updates.
Performance degradation due to sequential execution of multiple diagnostic checks.
issues.notes: This tool acts as an aggregation point for various quality checks, simplifying LLM interaction.

references.title: go-tools (Staticcheck): The advanced Go linter
references.why: Staticcheck is a widely used and highly regarded Go linter. Its implementation and comprehensive set of checks provide a strong reference for developing robust diagnostics and linting capabilities within 'modex'.

references.title: golangci-lint: Fast linters runner for Go
references.why: golangci-lint aggregates multiple Go linters and is a standard tool for Go code quality. Understanding its architecture and how it integrates various linters can inform the design of 'modex''s `get_diagnostics` tool and its integration with existing Go tooling.

references.why: Gokart is a dedicated static analysis tool for securing Go code. It can provide valuable insights into identifying security vulnerabilities programmatically, which is a key requirement for 'modex''s `get_security_diagnostics` tool.

issues.title: Implement MCP Tool: `get_build_diagnostics` (Compilation Errors)
issues.objective: Implement the `get_build_diagnostics` MCP tool to provide LLMs with specific feedback on compilation errors and other build-related issues in Go code.
issues.problem: LLMs frequently generate Go code with compilation blockers such as missing imports, incorrect assignments, or misuse of test packages. A dedicated tool is needed to capture and report these errors in a structured format.
changes: Define the `get_build_diagnostics` tool within the MCP server, accepting target file paths or module roots.
Implement the tool's logic to execute `go build` or `go test` commands in a controlled environment.
Capture and parse the standard error (stderr) output from these commands to extract structured error messages.
Format the parsed build errors, including file path, line number, column number, and error message, into a clear, LLM-consumable response.
issues.verification: The `get_build_diagnostics` tool should accurately identify and report compilation errors when invoked on Go code with known build issues. The output should precisely indicate the location and nature of each error.
out_of_scope: Fixing compilation errors automatically.
Providing detailed suggestions for resolving specific compilation issues (this would be part of LLM's reasoning or other tools).
acceptance_criteria: The `get_build_diagnostics` MCP tool is registered and callable.
When run on Go code with deliberate compilation errors, the tool returns a structured list of errors.
Each error in the report includes the file path, line, column, and a descriptive message.
When run on valid Go code, the tool returns an empty error list.

new_tests: Create a temporary Go file with a missing import statement and verify `get_build_diagnostics` reports it accurately.
Create a temporary Go file with a syntax error (e.g., undeclared variable) and verify the tool identifies it.
Test with a correctly compiling Go file to ensure no false positives are reported.
testing_strategy.test_patterns: Standard Go testing practices using `_test.go` files and `go test ./...`.

research_questions: How can `go build` output be parsed most robustly across different Go versions and error message variations?
risks: Variations in `go build` output format could lead to brittle parsing logic.
Execution environment differences might affect build command behavior.
issues.notes: Addressing compilation blockers is a direct response to a major LLM failure mode.

validation.method: Go unit tests executing `go build` on test cases

issues.title: Implement MCP Tools: `get_modernize_diagnostics` and `apply_modernize`
issues.objective: Provide LLMs with the ability to identify and apply `go fix` transformations through `get_modernize_diagnostics` and `apply_modernize` MCP tools, addressing stale Go idioms.
issues.problem: LLMs often generate Go code that uses stale idioms or deprecated APIs. 'modex' needs to guide them towards modern practices by providing diagnostics and a mechanism to automatically apply `go fix` transformations.
changes: Define the `get_modernize_diagnostics` MCP tool. Implement its logic to run `go fix -diff ./...` on the target code and parse the diff output to highlight suggested modernizations.
Define the `apply_modernize` MCP tool. Implement its logic to execute `go fix ./...` on specified files or packages, applying the modernization transformations directly.
Consider programmatic integration with the `go/analysis` framework for finer-grained control over transformations, if shelling out to `go fix` proves insufficient.
issues.verification: The `get_modernize_diagnostics` tool should accurately report suggested `go fix` changes on code with outdated idioms. The `apply_modernize` tool should successfully transform the code according to `go fix` rules.
out_of_scope: Developing custom code modernization rules (rely on `go fix` or `go/analysis` analyzers).
Handling conflicts or edge cases during `apply_modernize` (defer to `go fix` behavior).
acceptance_criteria: Both `get_modernize_diagnostics` and `apply_modernize` MCP tools are registered and callable.
When `get_modernize_diagnostics` is run on Go code with outdated idioms, it returns a clear report of suggested changes.
When `apply_modernize` is run on such code, the code is modified to reflect modern Go practices.
Applying `apply_modernize` to already modern code results in no changes.

new_tests: Create a temporary Go file containing a construct that `go fix` can modernize (e.g., `bytes.Compare` to `bytes.Equal` for `== 0`). Assert `get_modernize_diagnostics` correctly identifies this.
Apply `apply_modernize` to the same file and verify the code is updated as expected.
Test both tools on a Go file that requires no modernization to ensure no unintended changes or reports.
testing_strategy.test_patterns: Standard Go testing practices using `_test.go` files and `go test ./...`.

research_questions: What are the limitations of `go fix` and when might programmatic `go/analysis` integration be necessary for more complex modernization tasks?
How can the `go fix -diff` output be parsed most effectively to provide LLMs with actionable insights?
risks: Automated code modification carries inherent risks of introducing new bugs or breaking functionality.
`go fix` might not cover all 'stale idioms' that LLMs produce, requiring additional custom analyzers.
issues.notes: Directly addresses the LLM failure mode of generating stale Go code.

references.title: adk-go: An open-source, code-first Go toolkit for building, evaluating, and deploying sophisticated AI agents with flexibility and control.
references.why: This project is a Go toolkit specifically designed for building AI agents and explicitly mentions LLMs and the Model Context Protocol (MCP). It provides a strong reference for how to structure a Go-native agent and integrate with LLM workflows.

references.title: rag-code-mcp: Semantic code navigation MCP server using RAG.
references.why: This project is an MCP server that supports Go and focuses on semantic code navigation using Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). This aligns well with 'modex''s goal of providing indexed documentation and comprehensive diagnostics to LLMs for better Go code generation, directly addressing LLM failure modes.

references.title: mcp-go: A Go implementation of the Model Context Protocol (MCP).
references.why: This project provides a concrete example of an MCP server implementation in Go. It can serve as a valuable reference for understanding the architecture and design patterns for building an MCP server using Go.

validation.method: Manual review of research document and discussion with project leads

assumptions: The Go 1.25+ development environment is stable and available for all tooling integrations.
The `github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk` provides sufficient abstractions for implementing the required MCP tools.
External Go tools like `go vet`, `go fix`, `govulncheck`, and linters will have stable command-line interfaces or programmatic APIs for integration.
The primary communication transport will be stdio, with HTTP/SSE as a potential future enhancement for specific use cases.
open_questions: What is the exact definition and expected behavior for each proposed MCP tool (`register_project`, `get_go_version_info`, etc.)?
What is the preferred approach for error reporting and structured output from MCP tools to LLMs?
How will the `modex` server be deployed and managed in an LLM-agent ecosystem (e.g., containerized, local binary)?
What specific external Go linters should be integrated, and what is the preferred method (shelling out, Go API)?
What are the performance characteristics and resource constraints for running multiple static analysis tools concurrently within the MCP server?
